Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz is the sweet spot for Days Gone on the Deck — the open world feels fluid and responsive, textures look good at Medium, and FSR from 1024x640 keeps the image clean. Horde encounters may dip briefly to 35 fps but recover quickly.

profiles.Summary: Days Gone is a Steam Deck Verified open-world action game that runs well on the hardware, though its demanding open-world environments and Freaker hordes push the RDNA 2 GPU hard, requiring lowered settings and FSR to maintain stable frame rates. With tuned settings it delivers a solid and enjoyable experience, landing between 30–45 fps depending on the profile.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (GTX 780 / GTX 1060), the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti GPU class, and the game's Steam Deck Verified status. On your first run, check frame times in an open-world area with foliage and during a Freaker encounter — if the Optimal profile dips below 35 fps consistently, switch to Max Battery settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 and an 8 W TDP cap keeps thermals and battery draw minimal; the 30 fps cap paired with a 40 Hz refresh rate eliminates tearing and feels smooth. Drop Crowd Density if horde scenes stutter below 25 fps.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapped TDP lets the APU boost fully; 60 fps is achievable in lighter areas but expect drops to 40–45 fps in dense forests and horde encounters, so consider dropping the cap to 45 if consistency matters more than peak smoothness. Battery life is short — best used plugged in or for shorter sessions.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap gives perfectly smooth, tear-free gameplay and a solid visual upgrade over Max Battery; FSR at 1024x640 keeps the GPU comfortable. This is the recommended daily driver profile for most players.
